name: Raffles Hotel Le Royal
positioning: Historic hotel built in 1929 on a tree-lined avenue in central Phnom Penh, with French colonial, Khmer and Art Deco influences
best_for: Travelers who want a historic hotel in central Phnom Penh
Guests interested in Cambodian royal recipes and modern Khmer cuisine
Gin and cocktail lovers drawn to the Elephant Bar

facts.text: It reopened as Raffles Hotel Le Royal in 1997 after extension and renovation.
The hotel is set on a tree-lined avenue in central Phnom Penh.
The hotel's style draws on French colonial, Khmer and Art Deco influences.
Rooms have high ceilings, wooden floors and marble bathrooms.
State Rooms have air-conditioning, overhead fans and windows that open for fresh air.
The Elephant Bar Gin Experience includes two hours of unlimited gin cocktails and a gin tasting.
The Elephant Bar has a daily happy hour with 40% off selected drinks between 6pm and 8pm.
Raffles Spa offers traditional Khmer and modern treatments.
The spa has male and female wet areas with saunas, steam rooms and Jacuzzi, plus an outdoor lap pool and fitness centre.
The signature Khmer massage, known as chad ta shai, is a vigorous, firm pressure point massage.
Afternoon Tea is served at the hotel.

highlights.text: Suites are named to honour Cambodia's history or four former residents: Charlie Chaplin, Jacqueline Kennedy, Charles de Gaulle and Somerset Maugham.
Many dishes at Restaurant Le Royal are made from recipes entrusted to the hotel by Cambodia's Royal Palace.
The Elephant Bar offers over 200 different types of gin, including its own locally crafted Elephant Bar Gin.
Landmark Rooms are in the 1929 historic building and have an original clawfoot bath.
Restaurant Le Royal is set beneath a handpainted ceiling.

considerations.text: The hotel names November to February as the best time to visit Phnom Penh, when the weather is cooler.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the heritage brand positioning.
WhataHotel notes the historic building has traditional room layouts.
